description: Use this when the user wants flashcards: made from notes, slides or a file they share, a topic they name, or this conversation, or to memorize something and review it later. Saves 1-500 cards into one deck of their Flash account (created if missing, with parents for Parent::Child), where spaced repetition schedules each card's reviews. Follow the field notes; cloze uses {{c1::answer}}; keep media as /media/{id}. To change existing cards use update_cards, not new copies.

say.description:
"equation" for a formula too long to read, "look" for anything
that cannot be said aloud.

back_html.description: The answer to exactly what the front asks, as short as it can be while complete. Anything more (why, an example, a source) comes after the answer, set apart.

back_speech.description: What is read aloud of this side, in order, as blocks: [{"lang":"en","text":"How do you say cat in Japanese?"},{"lang":"ja","text":"ねこ"}]. Follow the side as it is written, in its order, never rewording it. Each block is one language, by ISO 639-1 code, with a region where the accent matters (es-MX, es-ES, pt-BR, pt-PT, en-GB); a word in another language inside a sentence is its own block where it stands. Leave out what is not read aloud: citations and sources, a romanization next to the script it spells (romaji, pinyin), emoji, images. Write a word as it is said when its spelling is ambiguous (Japanese kanji in kana, 猫 as ねこ; Chinese in simplified characters). A short formula of a few symbols in words (F = ma as "F equals m a"); a long one as {"say":"equation"}; anything that cannot be said aloud, Cantonese included, as {"say":"look"}.

front_html.description: The prompt, answerable on its own: one question, cue or cloze sentence carrying everything needed to answer it (the choices of a multiple-choice question, the context a case depends on). One idea per card: a list, a multi-part rule or a comparison becomes several cards, or a cloze with one blank per part.

front_speech.description: What is read aloud of this side, in order, as blocks: [{"lang":"en","text":"How do you say cat in Japanese?"},{"lang":"ja","text":"ねこ"}]. Follow the side as it is written, in its order, never rewording it. Each block is one language, by ISO 639-1 code, with a region where the accent matters (es-MX, es-ES, pt-BR, pt-PT, en-GB); a word in another language inside a sentence is its own block where it stands. Leave out what is not read aloud: citations and sources, a romanization next to the script it spells (romaji, pinyin), emoji, images. Write a word as it is said when its spelling is ambiguous (Japanese kanji in kana, 猫 as ねこ; Chinese in simplified characters). A short formula of a few symbols in words (F = ma as "F equals m a"); a long one as {"say":"equation"}; anything that cannot be said aloud, Cantonese included, as {"say":"look"}.

note_type.description: basic (default): one question, one answer. basic_reversed: both directions are worth asking (a word and its translation, a term and its definition). basic_typed: the exact spelling, number or formula matters. cloze: a sentence whose blanks are each their own fact, {{c1::...}}, {{c2::...}}.

description: Use this when the user wants to study, review, practice, be quizzed on or drill their flashcards, including cards made moments ago. Starts a spaced-repetition session over the cards due now: all of them, one deck (with its subdecks), or the cards carrying every given tag (list_tags has the names). Progress counts only for cards asked here and graded with submit_review, so ask each card from this session, never from the conversation. To make new cards use create_cards. Returns the first card's front (ask it and wait for the user's answer), how many cards are due, and grading_mode. Render front_html for display or interpret it for speech; present cloze gaps without revealing answers, and never read raw markup or URLs aloud. Fetch media URLs with the connector Bearer token if needed. Follow grading_mode for the whole session. Internal fields (ids, counts) are never read aloud.

description: Use this after the user answers the card just asked in a study session: records how well they knew it, which sets when the card comes back, and returns the next card. Grade STRICTLY against the card's back: facts, numbers, doses, and units must match precisely. An imprecise answer is 1 (Again), never 'close enough'; only phrasing may differ. Part of an answer is a miss, so '60' for '60 to 100 bpm' is 1. 1=Again (wrong, blank, or anything the card asks for left out), 2=Hard (the whole answer, but slowly or unsurely), 3=Good (the whole answer), 4=Easy (the whole answer at once). 2, 3 and 4 all record that the user knew it. State the exact answer on a miss, then immediately ask next_card's front. A null next_card ends the session. Wrap up briefly.

card_id.description: The card just asked: the card_id of the front the user answered.

name: submit_review

CardFrontOut.description: Rich question only. Editable source is deliberately absent during study.

next_card.description: Next card to ask immediately, or null when the session is finished.

note.description: Present only when the queue is empty: why, and what to do next.

title: Submit review

description: Use this when the user wants to study an archived deck again. Puts it back into study: its cards come back with the review history they had, so whatever came due while it was archived is due now, within the daily limits. Its subdecks come back with it, and so do the decks it sits in.

deck.description:
The deck's full name, e.g. "Pharm::Cardio" (list_decks has the
names).

name: unarchive_deck
title: Unarchive deck

description: Use this when the user asks to fix, reword, correct or retag cards they already have. Changes 1-500 cards atomically: give card_id and only the fields to change (front_html, back_html, tags); the rest stay, cards keep their schedule and review history, and restore_cards can undo the edit. Read list_cards first; for a shared source copy its sibling_card_ids, one edit per source. The note type stays; an edit that would remove cards is refused (use delete_cards). Follow create_cards' field notes.

back_html.description: The answer to exactly what the front asks, as short as it can be while complete. Anything more (why, an example, a source) comes after the answer, set apart.

back_speech.description: With a back_html it changes: the new back's speech blocks.

card_id.description: The card to change, from list_cards.

front_html.description: The prompt, answerable on its own: one question, cue or cloze sentence carrying everything needed to answer it (the choices of a multiple-choice question, the context a case depends on). One idea per card: a list, a multi-part rule or a comparison becomes several cards, or a cloze with one blank per part.

front_speech.description:
With a front_html it changes: the new front's speech blocks (see
create_cards).

sibling_card_ids.description:
Every card made from this card's source, this card included,
exactly as list_cards shows them in source.sibling_card_ids. Needed
when the source makes more than one card (a reversed pair, a cloze
with several gaps).

tags.description: A few short lowercase topic words (a chapter, a lesson, a theme), so the user can study one part later.

say.description:
"equation" for a formula too long to read, "look" for anything
that cannot be said aloud.

lang.description:
The language the words are in: an ISO 639-1 code, with a region
where the accent matters ("es-MX").

text.description: The words, as they are said.

SpeechBlockArg.description: One block of what is read aloud: words in one language, or a cue.

cards.description:
On both sides keep the material's own terms, names and numbers. Write what plain text loses as HTML (105, not 105; H2O;
between lines), and write each text in one script, as the material or the user writes it, never switching alphabets inside a word.

name: update_cards

note.description:
How to reply when the cards are already on screen; on new cards,
also where else the user can study them.

revision_ids.description:
One per source in source_ids: the earlier version of that source
this edit kept, which restore_cards can put back; null when the
edit changed nothing.

title: Update cards
